title: MotorLab StudyBook AI LAB101 qualitative review of first-read priority separation
reviewMethod: Assistant inspection of complete 56 model claims, source quotations, five page texts, and 53 hand-labeled LAB100 references; not independent academic, medical or legal expert validation.

pages.assessment: Scientific source negations (distance vs seasons, not every lunation) and causal connections all classified fundamental. One light/dark explanation as support.
issues: The model's semantic statements still require natural-language inference review. An atom of support may need explanatory coverage at the 10%-20% levels; do not simply delete it.

pages.editorialOverlap: 8/10 aligned labels match; 1 legacy atom unmatched due extraction segmentation
pages.assessment: Detected material under-prioritization of C4: who received a book and when was labeled support. Entire source concept C4 had no fundamental fact.
issues: Core fact F11 on recipients/dates was marked support although it is central to the register procedure.
Fact F12 «registro non contiene opinioni» is support despite a negation; requires human classification review, not automatic deletion.
A contextual opening was split into two facts, altering exact comparison to LAB100.
An internal obligation may be expressed by model wording of different strength, requiring source-based semantic review.

pages.editorialOverlap: 13/14 aligned labels match; one new context fragment
pages.assessment: Details include alveolar thin walls (support) and inspiration thoracic expansion (fundamental according to Gemini, support according to manual comparison). The differing rank is a judgment call, not proof of a factual error.
issues: The claim about measured values is close to source meaning, but degree of obligation and diagnostic caution should be checked before publication.
Source evidence validates where the claim came from, not whether every causal link is medically correct.

pages.assessment: Source comparison of documents was assigned to support while the goal of reconstructing events was fundamental; consequences and causes were promoted to core relative to editorial ranking.
issues: Several disagreements reflect a reasonable alternative grouping, and one could drop a distinct fact if a future short summary treats support as optional.
No whole-book context validation was performed.

pages.assessment: All three facts being fundamental is reasonable for an original page of only two sentences; no rule should force artificial support/context tiers for brief pages.
issues: Percent reduction remains nonbinding for original short pages; no automated PDF page-boundary test.

conclusion: LAB101 supports single-call extraction and three-way priority ranking on five synthetic pages. It cannot yet serve as a release gate: rank mistakes can demote entire concepts, lexical anchors do not establish semantic entailment, and no actual six compressed texts were generated. A separate concept-level and risk-word QA gate is required before any automatic use.
